extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, Federal Exchange operators, health insurance issuers, State governments, and public commenters on ACA Exchange and QHP rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: This page is a Federal Register proposed rule (HHS/CMS) describing proposed regulatory changes to Exchange operations, actuarial value (AV) de minimis ranges, eligibility definitions (including DACA), information collection burdens, and associated cost/burden estimates for plan years beginning 2026 and later. It solicits public comment on these proposals and the underlying estimates/methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contribution percentage calculation (§155.605(d)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The required contribution percentage is calculated using the excess of the rate of premium growth between the preceding calendar year and 2013, over the rate of income growth for that period, applied to the initial 2014 required contribution percentage (8 percent). For PY 2026 the calculation uses NHEA per capita personal income projections for 2013 and 2025 and the proposed PY 2026 premium adjustment percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses NHEA Projections 2023-2032 per capita PI values carried out to ten significant digits; example calculation shown resulting in a proposed PY 2026 required contribution percentage of 8.05 percent (8.00 × 1.0060718427). The required contribution percentage continues to determine affordability exemptions (e.g., for catastrophic coverage eligibility for ages 30+). CMS will publish the required contribution percentage in guidance by January of the year preceding the plan year unless methodology is amended through notice-and-comment rulemaking. CMS seeks comment on reverting to the premium adjustment percentage methodology finalized in the 2020 Payment Notice (using private health insurance premiums excluding Medigap and P&C insurance) and on the proposed PY 2026 value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing by income tier (PY 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed PY 2026 reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing varies by household income: a reduction for enrollees with household income >=100% and <=200% FPL; a 1/5 (one-fifth) reduction for enrollees with household income >200% and <=250% FPL; and no reduction for individuals with household incomes >250% and <=400% FPL for PY 2026 (as displayed in Table 8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule displays the resulting proposed PY 2026 reduced maximum annual limitations on cost sharing in a table (Table 8). Comment is sought on the PY 2026 reduced maximum annual limitations and the underlying proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actuarial value (AV) de minimis ranges for metal levels (§156.140(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed change to the de minimis AV ranges beginning in PY 2026: +2/−4 percentage points for all individual and small group market plans subject to the AV requirements under the EHB package (standard metal levels), except expanded bronze which is proposed to have +5/−4 percentage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains history: prior ranges varied (+2/−2, +5/−2 for expanded bronze, +2/−4 during PYs 2018–2022, narrowed in PY 2023). Rationale: revert to earlier ranges to balance comparability between levels and issuer flexibility, promote competition, allow more permissive plan AV designs while noting issuers can still design plans closer to the middle of ranges. CMS seeks comment on this proposed change.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis variation for expanded bronze plans
rubrics_metrics.description: For expanded bronze plans, propose de minimis AV range of +5/−4 percentage points beginning in PY 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restores the expanded bronze flexibility previously allowed (referenced 2018 Payment Notice). CMS believes this promotes issuer flexibility and market stability. Seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove de minimis certification requirement for individual market silver QHPs (§156.200(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to §156.200(b)(3) to remove from QHP certification conditions the de minimis range of +2/0 percentage points for individual market silver QHPs, reverting to the 2012 Exchange Establishment rule language requiring compliance with benefit design standards in §156.20.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS rationale: the +2/0 certification requirement (from 2023 Payment Notice) is no longer considered in the best interests of the overall risk pool because although it maximizes PTC/APTC for subsidized consumers, it harms affordability for unsubsidized consumers and reduces issuer flexibility, potentially damaging market stability. CMS seeks comment on removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis variation for income-based silver CSR plan variations (§156.400)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed revision to the definition of 'de minimis variation for a silver plan variation' to change the de minimis variation for individual market income-based silver CSR plan variations from +1/0 percentage points to +1/−1 percentage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes this change (along with removing the silver QHP certification requirement) would balance affordability and market stabilization. CMS does not propose edits to the required minimum 2 percentage point AV differential for 73% income-based plan variations in §156.420(f); standard silver QHPs with AVs 71–72% would still require the 73% variation to be at least 2 percentage points higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum AV differential requirement for 73% income-based silver variations (§156.420(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: No proposed changes: the AVs for silver QHPs and 73% income-based plan variations must differ by at least 2 percentage points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explicitly notes it is not proposing edits to this minimum differential and provides operational note for issuers about required AV relationships when standard silver QHPs fall at certain AVs (71–72%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability dates for finalized provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposals, if finalized, would be applicable beginning on or after January 1, 2026; others would be applicable upon the effective date of the final rule; specific timing noted for certain proposals (e.g., some proposals applicable beginning PY 2026, others upon effective date, and some beginning with annual redeterminations for PY 2027).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: proposed provisions requiring Exchanges to conduct pre-enrollment verification for SEPs and verify at least 75% of new enrollments via SEPs, and proposed prohibition on issuers covering sex trait modification as EHB would be applicable for plan years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026. Proposal to prevent automatic re-enrollment with APTC covering full premium without confirmation would be applicable starting with redeterminations for PY 2027. CMS seeks comment on whether regulated entities would require additional time to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchanges conduct pre-enrollment verification of SEP eligibility and verify 75% of new SEP enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed requirement that all Exchanges conduct pre-enrollment verification of eligibility for individual market Special Enrollment Periods (SEPs) and to verify at least 75 percent of new enrollments through SEPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, applicable on or after Jan 1, 2026. CMS believes this promotes program integrity and seeks comment on operational considerations and implementation hurdles for States and issuers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on issuers covering sex trait modification as an EHB
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed prohibition on issuers of coverage subject to EHB requirements covering sex trait modification as an essential health benefit (EHB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, applicable for plan years beginning on or after Jan 1, 2026. CMS seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent automatic re-enrollment with full APTC without enrollee confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed policy to prevent enrollees from being automatically re-enrolled in coverage with APTC that fully covers their premium unless the enrollee takes an action to confirm their eligibility information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, applicable starting with annual redeterminations for PY 2027. CMS argues this change protects Federal tax dollars and increases program integrity; seeks comment on operational impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal monthly SEP for APTC-eligible individuals at or below 150% FPL
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed repeal of the monthly Special Enrollment Period (SEP) for APTC-eligible qualified individuals with projected annual household income at or below 150 percent of the FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states experience suggests the SEP substantially increased improper enrollments and adverse selection; this proposal is intended to increase program integrity and protect Federal funds. If finalized, this provision would become applicable upon the effective date of the final rule. CMS seeks comment on operational effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS intends the rule's provisions, if finalized, to be severable from each other such that if any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, other provisions remain effective where possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS gives examples of distinct programs in the rule to show independent operability and solicits comment on severability. If a provision is found utterly invalid, HHS intends that provision to be severable.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRA public comment solicitation topics for information collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Paperwork Reduction Act, HHS solicits public comment on: (1) the need for the information collection and its usefulness; (2) the accuracy of the estimate of information collection burden; (3) the quality, utility, and clarity of the information to be collected; and (4) recommendations to minimize the information collection burden including automated techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS requests comment on each of these issues for specific sections of the document that contain information collection requests (ICRs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wage and opportunity cost estimation methodology for ICR burden
rubrics_metrics.description: To derive wage estimates, CMS generally uses Bureau of Labor Statistics data and doubles employee hourly wage estimates (100 percent increase) to approximate fringe benefits and overhead; adopts an after-tax hourly value of time for opportunity cost based on usual weekly earnings adjusted for estimated effective tax rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: started with usual weekly earnings $1,185 divided by 40 = pre-tax hourly $29.63, adjusted down by 17% tax to post-tax hourly $24.59. CMS seeks comment on these estimates and assumptions and cites ASPE guidance on valuing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: ICR burden and cost estimates for excluding DACA recipients from 'lawfully present' (BHP and Exchanges)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated system update burdens and costs: for two States operating a BHP (Minnesota and Oregon), assume 100 hours per State to update BHP eligibility and verification systems (25 hours database/network admin @ $101.66/hr; 75 hours programmer @ $95.88/hr) totaling 200 hours and $19,465. For Exchanges: estimate 1,000 hours per State Exchange to develop and code eligibility system changes (250 hours admin @ $101.66/hr; 750 hours programmer @ $95.88/hr) and corresponding costs; aggregate estimates provided (e.g., 20 State Exchanges × 1,000 hours = 20,000 hours at $1,946,500; Federal Government 1,000 hours at $97,325; total 21,000 hours at $2,043,825).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains assumptions (informed by FFE prior experience), conservative rounding, and solicits comment on these burden estimates. Also provides termination operation estimates for ending coverage for DACA recipients in FFEs/SBE-FPs and affected State Exchanges (e.g., 17,000 hours and $1,654,525 for States, plus Federal costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange application processing and assistance burden estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated time and per-application costs for assisting applicants and processing applications: government programs eligibility interviewer assumed 10 minutes (0.17 hours) at $48.34/hr → ~$8.22 per application. Application completion times: 30 minutes (0.5 hours) for those applying for insurance affordability programs and 15 minutes (0.25 hours) for those applying without consideration for such programs. CMS provides aggregate burden and cost savings estimates tied to the projected reduction in applicants due to proposed DACA changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS uses internal data and distribution assumptions (e.g., 98% of impacted would apply for affordability programs) to estimate opportunity cost savings using the $24.59 per-hour opportunity cost and to compute reductions in hours and dollars (e.g., net annual cost savings ~$133,870, reduction of ~5,445 hours). CMS seeks comment on these estimates and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estimates of enrollment and documentation impacts from DACA-related proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS estimates that, as a result of the proposed definition change for 'lawfully present,' approximately 11,000 fewer individuals would complete the application, 10,000 fewer would enroll in QHP coverage and 1,000 fewer in a BHP on average each year (including redeterminations/re-enrollments). Of the 11,000, about 80% (8,800) could have been electronically verified and 20% (2,200) would have required supporting documentation; about 2,000 would have generated an immigration status inconsistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS translates these figures into burden reductions for processing applications and adjudicating inconsistencies (e.g., 400 fewer inconsistency adjudication hours, cost savings of $19,336), and apportions savings between Federal and State Exchanges using a 49% (Federal)/51% (States) split of applications. CMS seeks comment on these estimates and assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to submit supporting documentation where lawful presence cannot be verified electronically (SAVE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges would require individuals completing the application to submit supporting documentation to confirm their lawful presence if it cannot be verified electronically via DHS SAVE (e.g., applicant opts not to include alien number or EAD number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS anticipates cost savings from reduced lawful presence inconsistencies if DACA recipients no longer apply; provides time estimate for consumers to gather/submit documentation (~1 hour) and associated opportunity cost ($24.59). Seeks comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology assumptions for apportioning application processing savings between Federal and State Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS uses 2024 Open Enrollment Period data showing 49 percent of Exchange applications submitted to FFEs/SBE-FPs (Federal) and 51 percent to State Exchanges to allocate application processing burden and savings between Federal Government (49%) and States (51%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS applies this split to estimate hours and cost savings attributable to each level of government (examples provided: reduction by 867 hours and $41,911 for State Exchanges; reduction by 833 hours and $40,267 for Federal Government). CMS requests comment on methodology and assumptions.
